{'paragraph': 'iPhone Duo will begin accepting pre-orders on Friday, October 16, but scammers are attempting to trick the public into visiting fake websites to place early orders.'}

{'paragraph': 'The malware-laden site is a remarkably faithful copy and claims to offer a US$500 discount coupon as an "exclusive authorized partner offer"…'}

{'paragraph': 'Researchers at cybersecurity firm Malwarebytes point out that the webpage uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which can compromise some older iPhones that have not been patched. Users do not need to take any action; simply visiting the site is enough to trigger the attack.'}

{'paragraph': 'If the attack succeeds, hackers will harvest your device identifiers and status information, and attempt to exfiltrate a list of installed apps along with the contents of your Apple Notes. Once that is done, they turn their attention to cryptocurrency wallets.'}

{'paragraph': 'The attack will also continue attempting to access your text messages, contacts, call logs, voicemail messages, email, calendar entries, and cached location data. The malware can also contact its server for additional instructions.'}

{'paragraph': 'The exploit chain was publicly disclosed by Google back in March this year, and Apple released a patch later the same month.'}

{'paragraph': '9to5Mac Take'}

{'paragraph': 'The usual precautions still apply. Do not click on links from unverified sources unless you trust the sender and were clearly expecting the message. And be sure to install iOS updates as soon as they become available.'}
